annotation.method: Codex read the complete 20-page source in physical order through Sections 1-8, Theorems 2.1-2.2, 3.1-3.2, 4.1, 6.2-6.3, Lemmas 5.1 and 7.2, Algorithms 6.1, 6.4, 7.1, 7.3, and 7.4, all numerical experiments, conclusions, and all 17 references; separated original proofs from cited matrix-function and norm-estimation results; audited Mathlib and the exact frozen 44-object NumStability surface; and compiled paired private feasibility proofs for the strongest self-contained candidate.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorem 2.1 and the Denman--Beavers derivative recurrence (2.4)-(2.5)
rejected_candidates.reason: The block-triangular function identity is quoted from Mathias and earlier sources, and convergence of the differentiated iteration is obtained by applying that cited identity together with cited convergence of the original Denman--Beavers iteration. Requiring either condition to rebuild those external results would not extract a proof supplied by P52.
Once the standard Fréchet chain rule is available, the fixed-point conclusion is the single displayed substitution in the paper and is below every tier's substantial-effort threshold.

The power-series formula in Theorem 3.1 is explicitly cited to an external source. Theorem 3.2 then applies the standard product rule to a monomial and takes norms term by term; its internally proved recurrence and bounds do not require a substantial compiled NumStability theorem and are below the T3 difficulty floor.

The polynomial-cost bound is a short structural induction: differentiating the final product adds two multiplications and the induction bounds the three smaller polynomials. The paper only remarks informally that shared dependencies benefit both evaluations equally. A stronger formal program-sharing theorem would require operational machinery and claims not stated or proved in P52, while the literal proof is below T3 difficulty.

The rational-derivative identity is one application of the product rule followed by rearrangement. The remaining section is an algorithmic framework and cost summary rather than a separate difficult correctness theorem.

Theorem 6.2 is recalled from the authors' earlier scaling-and-squaring error analysis. For Theorem 6.3, paired exact private proofs formalizing recurrence (6.4), the differentiated doubling identity (6.2), dyadic scaling, and the arbitrary-s induction compile in 67 N lines and 68 L lines. Their mathematical bodies are identical and L invokes no NumStability declaration. Thus the new induction has no library shortcut but is well below the required T2-or-harder T3 floor. Algorithm 6.4 packages these formulas and tabulated symbolic parameters; it is not accompanied by a stronger independent exact theorem.

Lemma 7.2 and the block 1-norm estimator are explicitly imported from earlier work. Algorithms 7.1, 7.3, and 7.4 combine those cited estimators with Algorithm 6.4, and the stated reliability and accuracy comparisons are empirical or inherited rather than new self-contained P52 proofs.

T1.decision: Skipped. The exact compiled library has matrix-exponential and operator-log infrastructure but no Fréchet derivative or differentiated scaling-and-squaring result. Its available exponential facts are either generic Mathlib-level support or correspond to background P52 cites; no internally proved P52 result needs exactly one substantial eligible shortcut.

T2.decision: Skipped. No internally proved P52 result receives two distinct substantial non-Mathlib shortcuts from the exact compiled library.

T3.decision: Skipped. The strongest self-contained new candidate, Theorem 6.3's arbitrary-step backward-error recurrence, compiles in a short paired proof and is below the T2 difficulty floor. Other internally proved claims are shorter, while the harder surrounding facts are cited, algorithmic, or empirical.

selection_policy: Use only exact claims and proof content established in P52.
Do not turn cited block-matrix, chain-rule, matrix-exponential backward-error, or norm-estimation results into P52 proof obligations.
Do not strengthen the informal dependency remark in Theorem 4.1 into a newly invented program-semantics theorem.
Do not convert tabulated symbolic parameters or numerical experiments into universal proof claims.
Assign a tier only after exact private N and L evidence establishes the tier criteria.
